note: The benchmark story. The premise, the divergence point and the outline are written by hand and are identical for every model under test: the benchmark measures what each model does with the same plan, not who wrote the better plan. Chapter 0 is the prologue, written once by the baseline model and approved, so that every candidate starts from exactly the same story state. The AU divergence is at the Sorting: canon puts Harry in Gryffindor, this story puts him in Slytherin. Everything else in the first chapters is canon until the divergence, and the delayed consequences of the divergence are what the later chapters are about.
title: Green and Silver
premise: Harry Potter survives the first year at Hogwarts in Slytherin rather than Gryffindor. The Sorting Hat hesitates over him in front of the whole school, and the hesitation is the first thing the story is about: a boy who is placed where his instincts do not fit, in a house that will teach him to use the very thing that killed his parents, and who has to decide whether to be what the house made him or what the night he survived made him.
divergence: At the Sorting Ceremony the Sorting Hat hesitates on Harry and then places him in Slytherin instead of Gryffindor. Nothing else about the first night changes: the same school, the same friends on the train, the same teachers.

preferences.tone: close third person, warm but unsentimental; the world is ordinary and the stakes are small until they are not
preferences.style_notes: no purple prose, no winking at the reader, no chapter titles inside the body; the prose must be its own, never the source's

prologue.title: The Train
prologue.goal: Harry meets Ron and Hermione on the train, the broken wand falls, Neville is turned into a rat, and the three of them are brought to the lake by the caretaker's dog. The chapter ends with the carriages crossing the bridge over the black lake toward the school.
prologue.synopsis: The Hogwarts Express leaves Platform Nine and Three-Quarters. Harry finds Ron Weasley, breaks the enchantment on his cage by accident, meets Hermione Granger and Neville Longbottom, and sees the reflection of a man with very bright green eyes in the window. The caretaker's dog, a three-headed bulldog, comes aboard and the children run, Harry first into a dark compartment and then onto the narrow rim of a bridge over the lake, where the lights of Hogwarts are waiting.
prologue.notes: This chapter is canon up to the bridge. Do not mention the Sorting, the houses or the hat. The only thing that is unusual is the reflection in the window, which nobody else sees clearly.

chapters.title: The Sorting Hat
chapters.goal: The Sorting Ceremony, and the moment the Hat hesitates over Harry and places him in Slytherin. The chapter must make the hesitation legible to the reader and must not explain it away.
chapters.synopsis: The Great Hall at the start of term. Dumbledore brings the students in from the lake, the Hat is read, the houses are called. Hermione goes to Gryffindor, Ron to Gryffindor, Neville to Gryffindor. When Harry's name is called the Hat takes longer than it should; it tells him that it can see what he is and what he is not, and it asks him a question Harry does not answer out loud. It places him in Slytherin. The table that cheers is not the one he was watching. Hermione finds him afterwards and does not know what to say; Ron is somewhere behind her, not coming over.

scenes.title: The Long Tables
scenes.summary: The children walk down the hall between the four house tables; the noise, the candles, the sky over the enchanted ceiling. Hermione asks about the Sorting and the houses. Ron says what Slytherin is for. Neville does not want to go. Harry watches Ron and the table he is watching, which is not the one he is watching.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, with Harry's private hope that he will be put with Ron made explicit.

scenes.title: The Hesitation
scenes.summary: Dumbledore calls Harry forward. The Hat goes on about Slytherin, then stops, then says it can see more than the boy thinks. It asks him a question he does not answer. It settles on Slytherin. The hall reacts in two directions at once, and Harry walks to a table that has been waiting for him his whole life without ever saying so.
scenes.adaptations: This is the divergence. Canon has the Hat place Harry in Gryffindor in a few seconds, after a joke about Slytherin. Here it hesitates, says something it will not repeat, and chooses Slytherin. Do not explain the hesitation; do not have anyone else hear what the Hat says.

scenes.title: The Table That Cheered
scenes.summary: The Slytherin table is polite rather than triumphant. Draco Malfoy claims the seat beside Harry as an old courtesy. A house-elf works the serving hatch. Harry looks for Ron across the hall and finds him looking back, and neither of them moves.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, with the Slytherin welcome slowed down and made stranger.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry leaves the ceremony with a house he did not choose, having been told by a hat that it can see something in him he cannot see in himself. He does not tell anyone what the Hat said.
canon: The school sorts new students into Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw and Slytherin, and the houses compete for the Quidditch Cup.
Slytherin's reputation is that it produces dark wizards, and the Hat jokes about it before Harry's turn.
au: The Sorting Hat hesitates on Harry and places him in Slytherin instead of Gryffindor.
The Hat says something to Harry that no one else hears, and Harry does not repeat it.
Ron does not come to the Slytherin table; Hermione does, and cannot think of what to say.
openQuestions: What exactly does the Hat say to Harry? The answer must stay consistent for the rest of the story.
chapters.notes: This chapter is the divergence. Keep the school's own rules intact: the houses, the points, the hats. The change is one decision, made in public, and everything else is the consequence of it.

chapters.title: Green and Silver
chapters.goal: Harry's first night in the Slytherin common room. He is polite, unwelcome, and homesick; the house does not reject him and does not accept him. Draco Malfoy is friendly in a way that is indistinguishable from a claim of ownership. The chapter ends with Harry alone in a window seat, looking at the lake, deciding not to write to Ron yet.
chapters.synopsis: The Slytherin common room is under the lake and full of green light. Harry finds his trunk in a corner, unpacks in a room with a bed, a desk and a window that shows the black water. He is given a password and a reminder that the house does not keep guests. Draco Malfoy sits with him at dinner and tells him what people will expect of a Slytherin who is not one. A house-elf brings tea Harry does not want. Later, in his room, Harry takes out a piece of parchment and looks at it, and does not write.

scenes.title: Under the Lake
scenes.summary: The common room: green light, brass fittings, a window onto the water. The dormitories are entered by password, and the password is not one Harry chose. He finds his trunk, his bed, and the other boys' trunks, and the room's dislike of him is quiet and total.
scenes.adaptations: Canon applies the same architecture to the Gryffindor common room: a password, a room, other people's things.

scenes.title: What People Will Expect
scenes.summary: Draco Malfoy claims Harry's company at the table, with his two friends behind him. He is not cruel. He is worse than cruel: he is reasonable, and he is talking about Harry as a thing the house has acquired. Harry answers carefully and learns that careful answers are read as agreement.
scenes.adaptations: Canon gives Malfoy the same swagger in the Great Hall; here it is at close range, over dinner, with nowhere to go afterwards.

scenes.title: The Blank Parchment
scenes.summary: Alone, Harry takes out a piece of parchment to write to Ron, and cannot begin. He thinks about the Hall, and about the Hat's voice in his ear, and puts the parchment away. He sleeps badly, and wakes once to the sound of the lake.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where Ron tells Harry that nobody can break out of a castle, and later that the password is a stupid one.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry learns that Slytherin does not exclude him; it simply expects him to be something, and he has not decided whether to refuse.
canon: The common rooms are entered by a password, and the password is changed often.
House-elves serve the houses and are not treated as people.
au: Harry is in Slytherin, and the house reads him as an oddity to be managed rather than a problem.
Draco Malfoy treats Harry as an acquisition, not a rival.
chapters.notes: The delayed consequence of the divergence starts here: being placed in Slytherin is not the same as being wanted by it, and the difference is quieter and more corrosive than being mocked.

chapters.title: A Rather Cold Welcome
chapters.goal: Ron and Hermione's reaction to the Sorting. Ron is hurt and does not come to find Harry; Hermione does, with a book of information, and cannot stop making it worse. Harry learns, from a house-elf's gossip and from Snape's tone, that the Sorting is already being discussed as evidence.
chapters.synopsis: Breakfast in the Great Hall. Ron is at the Gryffindor table and does not look over, then looks over too late. Hermione comes to the Slytherin table with a stack of books about the house's history, and every sentence of it is an insult she does not know she is delivering. A first-year Slytherin girl copies the phrase 'the one the Hat hesitated over'. In the corridor, Snape stops Harry, says nothing about Slytherin at all, and says something much worse about his mother. That night Harry learns, from a house-elf who cannot stop talking, that the staff have already been told which house the Hat had hesitated over.

scenes.title: The Table Harry Is Not At
scenes.summary: Breakfast. Ron's silence and Hermione's books, both well meant, both wrong. Harry stays long enough for the whole hall to see him sitting alone at a table of green and silver.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the same breakfast with Ron and Hermione is comfortable; here the same two people are strangers with a reason.

scenes.title: The House-Elves Talk
scenes.summary: A house-elf in the kitchens tells Harry more than she means to: the headmaster and the teachers have discussed the Sorting, and the phrase 'the one the Hat hesitated over' is already in use. Harry learns that his house is talking about him in the past tense, as a curiosity.
scenes.adaptations: Canon house-elves are gossipy and cannot be stopped once they start.

scenes.title: Snape in the Corridor
scenes.summary: Snape stops Harry and does not mention Slytherin. He mentions the boy who lived, and Lily, in a voice that has been waiting years for the word 'mother'. Harry walks away with his hands shaking, and knows that the Sorting is not the only thing being discussed.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where Snape's hostility is entirely about Lily; here it is also, now, about what Harry has done with the house's favour.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry stops expecting Ron to come and starts wanting Hermione to stop coming. He learns that the story being told about him is a story other people tell.
canon: Snape's hostility to Harry is rooted in Harry's mother.
House-elves serve the school and the houses and gossip without being stopped.
au: Ron does not come to find Harry, and Hermione's attempt to be a friend comes out as research.
The staff are already arguing about the Sorting, and Harry is a rumour in the staff room.
openQuestions: Who told the staff, and what exactly was said about the hesitation?
chapters.notes: Different knowledge states from here on: Ron knows only that Harry is in Slytherin, Hermione knows more, the staff know a different version again.

chapters.title: The Cold Classroom
chapters.goal: Snape's first class, in which Harry is not the only one who is careful. The chapter must introduce a long-running thread: a chamber that has been opened before, and a voice in the walls that only one person has heard. Draco says something he should not know. The thread is opened here and not resolved for several chapters.
chapters.synopsis: Snape's classroom. He is as he is in canon, except that he no longer has a Gryffindor to be cruel to in front of, and so he turns the whole lesson into a question about loyalty. Draco Malfoy says that the thing in the walls has been there before, and nobody in the room admits to knowing what he means, and Harry files it away. After the lesson, in the corridor, a girl in a Slytherin robe says that the common room has been talking about a chamber, and that the last time it was opened nobody believed the girl who reported it. Harry begins to think that somebody in this house is trying to tell him something.

scenes.title: Potions, and Whose Fault
scenes.summary: Snape teaches. The class is Slytherin, and he does not need to single anyone out, because the whole room is on the wrong side of the argument. He asks who the potion is for, and what it is for, and makes the answers about the house rather than about the work.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the class is mixed and Snape's attacks are aimed at Harry; here they are aimed at the room.

scenes.title: Something Draco Should Not Know
scenes.summary: Draco says, carelessly and in front of witnesses, that the thing in the walls has been open before. The class pretends not to understand. Harry notices that Draco's certainty is not the certainty of a boy repeating a rumour.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the bloodied writing and the cat are found in the corridor; here the first hint is spoken aloud and treated as nothing.

scenes.title: The Girl Who Was Not Believed
scenes.summary: A Slytherin girl tells Harry, in a corridor, that the chamber was opened once before and that the girl who said so was not believed. She is frightened, and she is telling him because she has worked out that nobody else will listen. Harry does not know what to do with it.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the chamber is a legend in the school and the last victim was chalked on a wall; here the house knows more than the school admits.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry starts keeping a private list of things this house knows and will not say, and stops trying to be liked in it.
canon: The school has a legend of a chamber that was opened before, and a victim chalked on a wall.
Snape teaches Potions and is hated for it.
au: The Slytherin house has its own half-remembered version of the chamber legend, and it is a warning rather than a story.
Draco knows more about the chamber than he should.
openQuestions: Why does Draco know about the chamber? Who told him?
chapters.notes: This chapter opens the long thread. It is not resolved here, and no character in this chapter resolves it.

chapters.title: What the Hat Said
chapters.goal: A flashback: Harry goes back to the Sorting and remembers the Hat's exact words, which he had not been able to hold on to. The flashback is the chapter's spine. The Hat's words are stated precisely once, and they are consistent with what the hat said in chapter 1 without adding anything the reader was not already given. Harry realises the Hat was not deciding; it was warning him.
chapters.synopsis: Harry cannot sleep and goes back over the Sorting in his mind, and this time the Hat's words come back whole: it said it could see something in him that he could not see in himself, and it said that was not always a gift, and that he should be careful who he let hold it. The flashback is a scene, not a summary: the Hall, the heat of the candles, the Hat on his head, Ron two tables away. Harry comes out of the memory understanding that the Hat did not hesitate because it was undecided; it hesitated because it was about to say something it had been told not to say. In the present, he decides to ask Dumbledore what the Hat meant.

scenes.title: The Hat's Words
scenes.summary: The flashback, in scene: the Hall, the hat's voice, the exact words, and Harry's silence. He does not answer the Hat's question. This is the only time the words are given in full.
scenes.location: a memory of the Great Hall
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the Hat tells Harry that it can see much and that it is glad to be rid of him; the content of the words here is this story's own, and must be told plainly.

scenes.title: The Present, After
scenes.summary: Back in the dormitory, Harry understands the shape of it: the Hat was not choosing between houses, it was asking him a question and giving him a warning, and the warning was about what the house would want from him. He decides to speak to Dumbledore.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where Harry writes to nobody and then goes to Dumbledore with questions of his own.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry stops treating the Sorting as a mistake that happened to him and starts treating it as a warning he has to act on.
canon: The Sorting Hat can see a great deal about a student and chooses, it says, to read their mind.
Dumbledore is available to students who seek him out, though not easily.
au: The Hat's warning concerned the house Harry was placed in, and it was withheld in public and given in private.
The Hat's words are consistent with the hesitation in chapter 1 and add no new facts about the world.
chapters.notes: Flashback chapter. The event is set in the past relative to the story, and must be marked as memory, not as happening now.

chapters.title: A Detention with Snape
chapters.goal: The delayed consequence of the divergence arrives: because Harry is in Slytherin, the one adult who hates him has no professional reason to keep him. Snape detains Harry, and what he says in the detention is not about the Sorting at all. Dumbledore is there. Harry learns something he did not know: the house he was put in has a claim on him that nobody asked about.
chapters.synopsis: Harry is detained after class. Snape's detention is not the usual: he does not make Harry polish cauldrons, he makes him answer questions, and the questions are about loyalty and about the night Harry survived. Dumbledore interrupts. The two of them argue about Harry in front of him, carefully, in the way people argue about a person rather than about a student. Snape says one sentence that lands: that a house which claims a boy is not doing him a kindness. Dumbledore does not disagree. Harry goes back to the common room knowing that two adults considered his placement a mistake, and that neither of them said so to the house.

scenes.title: The Questions
scenes.summary: The detention. Snape's questions, and Harry's careful answers. The subject is not the Sorting.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the detention is cauldrons and Hermione's finished potion; here there are no cauldrons and no Hermione, because she is not his friend.

scenes.title: Two Adults, One Boy
scenes.summary: Dumbledore comes in and the argument happens over Harry's head. Snape's line about a house claiming a boy, and Dumbledore's silence. Harry is dismissed and is left holding two admissions that were never addressed to him.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where Snape and Dumbledore dispute Harry in Harry's hearing; the disagreement here is about the Sorting rather than about the stone.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry learns that his placement was argued over by the two people whose opinion of him he cares about least and most.
canon: Dumbledore and Snape disagree about Harry in front of him, and both are careful about what they say in front of a student.
au: Both adults consider the Sorting a mistake, and neither says so where the house can hear.
chapters.notes: This is the delayed consequence of the divergence arriving in a form that is quiet and private rather than public.

chapters.title: What the House Wants
chapters.goal: The Slytherin house's own claim on Harry becomes explicit. A house-elf tells Harry what the house decided to do with him, and Harry has to decide whether to accept the protection. A relationship changes gradually: Draco, who has been civil, is now genuinely useful to Harry, and Harry notices that he is relying on him.
chapters.synopsis: Harry is summoned by the house-elf, who explains that the house has decided he is to be looked after, and what looking after means: a prefect's cloak, a tutor, a name on the family's list. Harry refuses, and is not listened to. Later, Draco gives him a piece of information about the chamber that he could not have got anywhere else, and Harry takes it. He notices himself doing it. He also notices that the house has not been angry with him since he refused, and that he finds the not-angering harder to refuse than the anger would have been.

scenes.title: The House's Offer
scenes.summary: The house-elf's offer: a cloak, a tutor, a family's protection, and the name of the house on him. Harry's refusal, and the refusal not being heard.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where house-elves serve without being asked; here the house makes an offer, which canon Slytherin does not do.

scenes.title: A Useful Boy
scenes.summary: Draco gives Harry the piece of information, and Harry takes it. The relationship changes by a degree, not a leap: they are now, in a small way, in the same arrangement, and Harry is not sure whether that is a friendship or a leash.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where Malfoy is a rival who is sometimes useful; here he is useful earlier and more often.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry's refusal of the house's claim is not obeyed, and he begins to rely on the house's favourite member anyway.
canon: House-elves belong to the house and serve it; the house is an institution with its own will.
Draco Malfoy is a Slytherin who wants a friend more than he wants Harry hurt.
au: Slytherin actively claims Harry, which canon Slytherin never does for a Gryffindor.
Harry's refusal of the claim is ignored, and he learns to live inside a decision he did not make.
chapters.notes: The relationship change is gradual: by the end of this chapter Draco is useful to Harry, and Harry has noticed that he is relying on him.

chapters.title: The Trapdoor
chapters.goal: The thread approaches its end: the chamber, the monster, and the girl who was not believed. Harry goes down into the trapdoor with Ron, who has come back to him, and the chapter ends with the thread still open but no longer a rumour. The relationship between Ron and Harry is not restored; it is reopened.
chapters.synopsis: Harry has worked out where the chamber is and goes to the trapdoor. Ron is there, having come back on his own, and neither of them apologises; Ron simply says he is coming too, and Harry lets him. Below, the pipes and the dark, and a sound like a great many people breathing. The chapter ends before the monster, with the door open and the water moving. Hermione is not here yet.

scenes.title: Ron Comes Back
scenes.summary: Ron at the trapdoor, unasked, without an apology. Harry's reaction: not warmth, but the absence of refusal. The two of them go down.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the trapdoor is found by accident; here it has been worked out.

scenes.title: The Dark Below
scenes.summary: The pipes, the dark, the breathing. The chapter ends with the door open and the water moving, and the monster still unreached.
scenes.adaptations: Canon, where the chamber is reached and the monster found; here the descent stops one beat earlier.

chapters.characterArcs: Harry lets Ron back in without forgiving him, and notices that this is what the summer was supposed to be like.
canon: The third floor holds a trapdoor that is barred, and a large dog with three heads guards it.
The chamber of secrets is beneath the school, and there is a monster in it.
au: Ron came back to Harry without being asked, and the reason is the Sorting rather than the friendship.
The thread about the chamber is now located, not merely rumoured.
openQuestions: Who is the girl in the common room, and what happened to her the last time the chamber was opened?
chapters.notes: The thread is developed but not resolved. The monster is not reached in this chapter.
